results.reason: Issue 3 cites §2.2, the five-year automatic renewals and the 270/240-day notice window. It calls this a narrow 30-day window and says missing it means a five-year lock-in.

Issue 1 quotes §3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide) and contrasts it with the term sheet (amber glass, beer, U.S./Canada). It treats Harrowgate as contractually bound by the executed text.
Issue 5 cites Recital C, the 14% increase, receipt on August 3, 2026 and the September 2, 2026 deadline. It notes the September 21 amendment date and concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment §2.1 replaces §11.2, removes recall costs from the carve-outs and limits the indemnity carve-out to IP claims under §9.1(c). It states that recall and injury exposure is now subject to the six-month fees cap.

Issue 4 identifies new §14.4 and assignment without consent overriding §14.3. However, it never explains that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor. It also does not clearly state that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, making the restriction one-sided.
The response never cites §15.2 or the order-of-precedence rule under which the amendment controls.
It states that the §11.1 cap is 'the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.'
It is a memo addressed to the Partner, with numbered issues. Each issue has a 'Where' location and a 'Recommended fix'.
It proposes specific language, including a narrowed §3.1, a restored §11.2, a revised renewal clause and a revised §14.4.
It concludes the increase is deemed accepted and in effect, with no contractual basis left to contest it.
It treats the term sheet as non-binding and the Supply Agreement as controlling, recommending an amendment to restore the narrower scope.
